name: Missed Train Dance: Miss the Train, Then Dance It Off, From One Photo
blurb: The missed train dance is the TikTok trend where you run for a train, the doors close in your face, you fall to your knees, and then you dance happily on the platform anyway.

prompts.label: 1. The video prompt is filled in. Settings: Seedance 2.5, 12 s, 720p, 9:16, sound on. The video prompt
prompts.text:
A viral "missed train dance" video made from [Image 1]: the person runs down the station stairs, the train doors close in front of them, they fall to their knees, then they stand up and dance happily on the platform. A handheld phone video filmed by a friend, vertical 9:16, photorealistic, real phone colors, one take with two quick whip pans.

The person in the video is the person in [Image 1], in every frame: copy the exact face from [Image 1] (the face shape, eye color and eye shape, eyebrows, nose, mouth, skin tone, age, hair color, hair length and hairstyle, and any beard, moustache, glasses or freckles), so their friends recognize them at once. The face stays the same from the first frame to the last, also while running and on the knees. They wear the clothes from [Image 1]; what the photo does not show is plain dark trousers and clean shoes.

THE PLACE: a modern underground train station at night, warm ceiling lights, a grey tiled floor, a concrete staircase with yellow-edged steps down to the platform, a yellow safety line along the platform edge. A long silver double-deck commuter train with bright yellow sliding doors stands at the platform. The train has no logo, no letters and no numbers on it. A few commuters far in the background, small and out of focus, all adults.

0-2.5 s: filmed from the bottom of the staircase, looking up: the person runs down the stairs toward the camera in a panic, one hand sliding on the rail.
2.5-4 s: a whip pan as they run past the camera onto the platform: the yellow doors slide shut right in front of them, one step too late. They stop at the yellow line, both arms out.
4-6.5 s: seen from behind, the closed yellow doors in front of them: they throw the head back and the arms wide in dramatic despair, then drop softly to their knees on the platform, lean forward and slide one leg out to the side, still behind the yellow line. The train starts to pull away.
6.5-8 s: they get up and turn to the camera, which is now close in front of them at chest height: a deadpan stare into the lens, the face large and sharp, the train gliding away behind them.
8-12 s: they break into a happy, loose, confident dance on the empty platform: shoulder bounces, hip sways, a little spin, both hands framing the face, a big carefree smile, then a final pose with a wink at the lens.

Audio: footsteps on the stairs, the door chime and the hiss of the doors closing, the train rolling away, then an original upbeat R&B dance beat with a deep bass from 6.5 s. No known song, no lyrics, no singing, no talking.

Exactly one person in focus, a grown adult; no famous people, no children. The person never crosses the yellow line, never touches the train or the doors, nobody is near the tracks. A soft, comic drop to the knees: no injury. One head, five fingers on each hand. No logos, no brand, no station name, no signs with words, no captions, no subtitles, no stickers, no watermark, no app interface.
